analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/reference/configuration.md. The patch adds two table rows at head lines 416-417: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED. Both are default-on, disabled by exact `0`, and forwarded to the LaunchAgent. The two supplied units (base lines 520-687 and head lines 1-353) do not display the changed lines 416-417, so I could not inspect the added rows directly. I relied on the patch excerpt, which is complete. No source code, keys, attestation, authorization or encryption logic changes. The base excerpt is unrelated surrounding text.

Security relevance:
- Streaming tool-call fragments as they are generated moves tool-call output earlier, but it stays on the existing per-request encrypted provider-to-coordinator response path. The doc states that each call is still validated when its frame closes. T-008 (fail closed on encryption failure) is not shown to be affected, but the underlying Swift implementation was not supplied. A reviewer of that code should confirm the streamed fragments go through the same encrypt-or-fail path and that invalid calls cannot reach the consumer after partial emission. That is an unverified implementation contract, not a finding.
- The think-content seeding changes reasoning-parser state for Qwen3-VL. It has no apparent confidentiality or authorization impact.
- The new env names are forwarded to the LaunchAgent. Only the kill-switch value `0` changes behavior, so this is limited to operator-local configuration, and the operator is already within the ADV-001 trust model (TB-003).

No threat-model assumption (T-041 prefix cache, the TB-011 App Attest boundary) is changed by this PR. The remaining head and base text is unchanged pre-existing documentation and is not re-reported.
